title: A lifted idempotent of A[T]/(f) lifts the coprime factorization of f
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal contained in the Jacobson radical of $A$, $f\in A[T]$ monic with image $\overline f\in(A/I)[T]$, and $\overline f=g_0h_0$ with $g_0,h_0\in(A/I)[T]$ monic and generating the unit ideal of $(A/I)[T]$. Let $B=A[T]/(f)$ and identify $B/IB$ with $(A/I)[T]/(\overline f)$ (reduction of coefficients). Let $\bar e\in B/IB$ be the idempotent with $\bar e\equiv1$ modulo $g_0$ and $\bar e\equiv0$ modulo $h_0$ (the element $(1,0)$ under the Chinese remainder isomorphism $(A/I)[T]/(\overline f)\cong(A/I)[T]/(g_0)\times(A/I)[T]/(h_0)$). If $e\in B$ is an idempotent whose image in $B/IB$ is $\bar e$, then there are monic polynomials $g,h\in A[T]$ with $f=gh$ whose images in $(A/I)[T]$ are $g_0$ and $h_0$. (In Stacks' proof, $g$ and $h$ are the characteristic polynomials of multiplication by $T$ on the finite locally free $A$-modules $eB$ and $(1-e)B$, which have constant ranks $\deg g_0$ and $\deg h_0$.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair, line 2553), proof of (3)$\Rightarrow$(1), from 'Set $B=A[T]/(f)$' to 'Details omitted. Thus (3) implies (1)': $B=eB\times(1-e)B$, $eB$ and $(1-e)B$ finite locally free of constant ranks $\deg g_0$, $\deg h_0$ (rank constant along $V(I)$ hence everywhere, as $I$ lies in the Jacobson radical), $f=\mathrm{CharPol}_A(T|B)=\mathrm{CharPol}_A(T|eB)\,\mathrm{CharPol}_A(T|(1-e)B)$, CharPol of a finite locally free module glued via Algebra Lemma 00EJ (lemma-standard-covering); 'Details omitted'

proof.text: *Setup.* Put $d=\deg f$, $n_1=\deg g_0$, $n_2=\deg h_0$ (natural degrees; if $A/I\neq0$ then $n_1+n_2=d$, as reduction preserves the degree of monic polynomials). By [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free], $B=A[T]/(f)$ is a free $A$-module with basis $1,t,\dots,t^{d-1}$ ($t$ the class of $T$), $B/IB\cong(A/I)[T]/(\overline f)$, and $(A/I)[T]/(g_0)$, $(A/I)[T]/(h_0)$ are free $A/I$-modules of ranks $n_1$, $n_2$ with bases the powers of the class of $T$. Since $g_0,h_0$ generate the unit ideal, $(g_0)\cap(h_0)=(g_0h_0)=(\overline f)$ and the Chinese remainder theorem gives an isomorphism of $(A/I)[T]$-algebras $\gamma:B/IB\cong(A/I)[T]/(g_0)\times(A/I)[T]/(h_0)$ with $\gamma(\bar e)=(1,0)$, $\gamma(1-\bar e)=(0,1)$; it is compatible with multiplication by $T$ on both sides.

source.place: Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair, line 2553), proof of (3)$\Rightarrow$(1), 'Set $B=A[T]/(f)$. Let $\overline e$ be the idempotent of $B/IB$ corresponding to the decomposition $B/IB=A/I[T]/(g_0)\times A/I[T]/(h_0)$' and 'Note that $B$ is free of rank $\deg(f)$ as an $A$-module'

proof.text: *The splitting $B=eB\oplus(1-e)B$ and its reduction.* As $e$ is idempotent and $B$ commutative, $B=eB\oplus(1-e)B$ as $B$-modules, hence as $A$-modules ($x=ex+(1-e)x$; $eB\cap(1-e)B=0$ since $y=ey'=(1-e)y''$ gives $y=ey=e(1-e)y''=0$). Multiplication by $t$, $\mu_t:B\to B$, preserves both summands; write $\varphi_1=\mu_t|_{eB}$, $\varphi_2=\mu_t|_{(1-e)B}$, so $\mu_t=\varphi_1\oplus\varphi_2$. Each summand is a direct summand of the finite free $A$-module $B$. Reducing modulo $I$: $IB=I\,eB\oplus I(1-e)B$, so $B/IB=eB/I\,eB\oplus(1-e)B/I(1-e)B$ and the first summand is the image of $eB$, i.e. $\bar e(B/IB)$. Hence $eB\otimes_AA/I=eB/I\,eB\cong\bar e(B/IB)\xrightarrow{\gamma}(A/I)[T]/(g_0)\times0$, an isomorphism of $A/I$-modules carrying $\varphi_1\otimes1$ to multiplication by $T$ on $(A/I)[T]/(g_0)$; likewise $(1-e)B\otimes_AA/I\cong(A/I)[T]/(h_0)$ carrying $\varphi_2\otimes1$ to multiplication by $T$. In particular $eB\otimes_AA/I$ and $(1-e)B\otimes_AA/I$ are free $A/I$-modules of ranks $n_1$ and $n_2$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair, line 2553), proof of (3)$\Rightarrow$(1), 'This gives a product decomposition $B=eB\times(1-e)B$'

proof.text:
*$eB$ and $(1-e)B$ are finite locally free of constant ranks $n_1$, $n_2$.* Let $P=eB$ (the case $(1-e)B$, $n_2$ is the same). By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-rank-locally-constant] ($P$ is a direct summand of the finite free $B$), $P_{\mathfrak p}$ is free over $A_{\mathfrak p}$ for every prime $\mathfrak p$ and $ho(\mathfrak p)=\operatorname{rank}_{A_{\mathfrak p}}P_{\mathfrak p}$ is locally constant on $\operatorname{Spec}A$. (a) For $\mathfrak p\supseteq I$: $\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}P\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)=ho(\mathfrak p)$, and also $P\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)=(P\otimes_AA/I)\otimes_{A/I}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ has dimension $n_1$ by step 2; so $ho=n_1$ on $V(I)$. (b) Let $Z=\{\mathfrak p:ho(\mathfrak p)
eq n_1\}$. Since $ho$ is locally constant, $Z$ and its complement are open, so $Z$ is closed, $Z=V(J)$ for an ideal $J$. If $Z
eq\emptyset$ then $J
eq A$, so $J\subseteq\mathfrak m$ for a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and $\mathfrak m\in V(J)=Z$. But $I$ lies in the Jacobson radical, so $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$, $\mathfrak m\in V(I)$ and $ho(\mathfrak m)=n_1$ by (a): contradiction. Hence $ho\equiv n_1$ on $\operatorname{Spec}A$. (c) By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-standard-free-cover] there are $f_1,\dots,f_r\in A$ generating the unit ideal with $P_{f_i}$ finite free over $A_{f_i}$, say of rank $m_i$. If $A_{f_i}=0$ then $P_{f_i}=0$ is free of rank $n_1$ too. Otherwise pick a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $A_{f_i}$, lying over $\mathfrak p\in D(f_i)$; then $P_{\mathfrak p}=(P_{f_i})_{\mathfrak q}$ is free of rank $m_i$ over $A_{\mathfrak p}=(A_{f_i})_{\mathfrak q}
eq0$, so $m_i=ho(\mathfrak p)=n_1$. Thus $P_{f_i}\cong A_{f_i}^{n_1}$ for all $i$: $eB$ is finite locally free of constant rank $n_1$, and $(1-e)B$ of constant rank $n_2$, in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-charpoly-locally-free]. (Stacks: 'since $eB$ and $(1-e)B$ have constant rank $\deg(g_0)$ and $\deg(h_0)$ over $A/I$ we find that the same is true over $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$'; (b) writes out why, using only that every nonempty closed subset of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ contains a maximal ideal.)

However, since $eB$ and $(1-e)B$ have constant rank $\deg(g_0)$ and $\deg(h_0)$ over $A/I$ we find that the same is true over $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$'; finite locally free from Algebra Lemma Tag 00NX

proof.text: *Definition of $g,h$ and $f=gh$.* Put $g=\mathrm{CharPol}_A(\varphi_1:eB\to eB)$ and $h=\mathrm{CharPol}_A(\varphi_2:(1-e)B\to(1-e)B)$ [def-weil-pbc-charpoly-locally-free], defined by step 3; by [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-locally-free-existence] $g=T^{n_1}+\dots$ and $h=T^{n_2}+\dots$ are monic. By [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-locally-free-direct-sum], $B=eB\oplus(1-e)B$ is finite locally free of constant rank $n_1+n_2$ and $\mathrm{CharPol}_A(\mu_t:B\to B)=gh$. On the other hand $B$ is itself free over $A$ (step 1); if $A\neq0$ its rank $d$ equals $n_1+n_2$ (compare ranks at any prime), and the characterizing property of [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-locally-free-existence] for the ring map $A\to A'=A$ says $\mathrm{CharPol}_A(\mu_t:B\to B)$ is the ordinary characteristic polynomial of $\mu_t$ on $B$, which is $f$ by [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-mul-T-monic-quotient]. Hence $f=gh$. (If $A=0$ every polynomial is $0$ and $f=gh$ trivially.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair, line 2553), proof of (3)$\Rightarrow$(1), 'We conclude that $f=\mathrm{CharPol}_A(T:B\to B)=\mathrm{CharPol}_A(T:eB\to eB)\,\mathrm{CharPol}_A(T:(1-e)B\to(1-e)B)$ is a factorization into monic polynomials'

proof.text: *Reductions modulo $I$.* Apply the characterizing property of [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-locally-free-existence] to $M=eB$, $\varphi=\varphi_1$, $n=n_1$ and the ring map $A\to A'=A/I$: by step 2, $eB\otimes_AA/I$ is free of rank $n_1$, so the image $\overline g$ of $g$ in $(A/I)[T]$ is the characteristic polynomial of $\varphi_1\otimes1$ on $eB\otimes_AA/I$. Under the isomorphism of step 2 with $(A/I)[T]/(g_0)$, $\varphi_1\otimes1$ becomes multiplication by $T$, and the characteristic polynomial is invariant under such an isomorphism (conjugate matrices have the same determinant $\det(T-\cdot)$; Mathlib LinearEquiv.charpoly_conj). By [lem-weil-pbc-charpoly-mul-T-monic-quotient] over the ring $A/I$ with the monic $g_0$, this characteristic polynomial is $g_0$. So $\overline g=g_0$, and likewise $\overline h=h_0$. Together with step 4: $g,h\in A[T]$ are monic, $f=gh$, and they reduce to $g_0,h_0$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_monic_factorization_of_idempotent {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I ≤ Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal A)) (f : A[X]) (hf : f.Monic) (g₀ h₀ : (A ⧸ I)[X]) (hg₀ : g₀.Monic) (hh₀ : h₀.Monic) (hcoprime : IsCoprime g₀ h₀) (hfactor : f.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) = g₀ * h₀) (e : AdjoinRoot f) (he : IsIdempotentElem e) (he₁ : AdjoinRoot.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) f g₀ (hfactor.symm ▸ dvd_mul_right g₀ h₀) e = 1) (he₀ : AdjoinRoot.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) f h₀ (hfactor.symm ▸ dvd_mul_left h₀ g₀) e = 0) : ∃ g h : A[X], g.Monic ∧ h.Monic ∧ f = g * h ∧ g.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) = g₀ ∧ h.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) = h₀
